newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bankers urge WTO financial services deal this year.
newsitem.headline: Bankers urge WTO financial services deal this year.

text.p: A coalition of North American and European bankers and businessmen called on Monday for a World Trade Organisation pact by the end of this year to open up the global financial services industry.

The appeal was launched by the coalition, the Financial Leaders Group, at the annual Davos World Economic Forum of political and business leaders and also aimed at negotiators at WTO headquarters in Geneva.

"Liberalisation of financial service markets ic critical to enhancing economic growth globally, regionally and for individual countries, both developed and developing," a statement from the group said.

Talks on a pact resume at the WTO in mid-April nearly two years after the United States pulled out of an earlier bid to shape an accord, arguing that offers from other countries were not enough to justify it opening up its own market.
After the U.S. decision, the European Union convinced other countries in the talks, including Japan, to agree to an interim deal pending a new round of talks this year.

Chairing the bank and business coalition, which has been holding meetings since last year to prepare the ground for the talks, are Andrew Buxton, Chairman of Britain's Barclays Bank, and Ken Whipple, President of the U.S. Ford Financial Services.

The group's statement said the interim accord "was a first constructive step forward" and provided the base for all countries to add the new commitments necessary for a global deal by the December 31 deadline.

It said the pact should provide for the right for foreign firms to establish local operations in signatory countries and to do business competitively, and establish that they should be treated on the same basis as domestic companies.

It also called for the lifting of most restrictions on provision of cross-border services, the reduction of barriers to the posting of key personnel, and common commitment that no new restrictions would be created.
Among other signatories of the appeal were executives of banks and firms based in Canada, France, Britain and Italy -- as well as the Chairman of Hong Kong's Trade Development Council, Victor Fung.
